ambiguityScan.justification: AC 4 ('opening a ticket and returning to the Tickets page restores the previous list state') admitted two honest readings of 'returning': (A) any navigation back to /tickets restores the state, requiring the global nav Tickets link (client/src/components/Layout.tsx:52) to carry preserved state and therefore a store of the last list URL outside the URL itself; (B) only retracing the path back — browser Back, or the ticket-detail back link (client/src/pages/TicketDetailPage.tsx:27) — restores it, while the global nav link keeps meaning 'fresh default list'. JB Mccallaghan resolved this to reading B at the spec gate on 2026-09-05. Reading B keeps the URL as the single source of truth, which is the story's own stated premise; reading A would have reintroduced non-URL list state. Layout.tsx:52 is therefore explicitly out of scope and the nav link continues to land on a clean /tickets.

e2e.note: First actual execution. Full suite run three times: 82/82 every time (4.3m, 2.4m, 3.9m); the 13 new scenarios 13/13. The third run was at this checks.commit; the first two were at 093cef0, whose tree differs only in .solvo and docs markdown (git diff --stat 093cef0..1174a2c touches no source or test file). This replaces an 'n/a' record that named the database credential as the sole blocker - it was not. playwright.config.ts started the client webServer with a POSIX 'VITE_API_URL=... bun run' prefix, and Playwright spawns webServer through the platform shell, so cmd.exe read VITE_API_URL as a program name and the suite could not start on Windows at all. Present since initial commit 65da45b and on main; this branch had never touched the file. Fixed via the webServer env field. Two further defects found by running them: CASE-6e5a5e6f195f failed 6 runs in 10 (a page.route pattern broad enough to park goBack()'s own request, then unroute racing the parked handlers into 'Route is already handled!') - now matched on sortBy=subject, 10/10, and non-vacuity confirmed by inverting the expected row order; and this story's 8 tests x 11 seeded tickets pushed tickets.spec.ts's and ticket-detail.spec.ts's own tickets off page 1 of an unfiltered list under fullyParallel, so workers:1 is now set. Attribution measured, not inferred: 69/69 in parallel with the new spec excluded, 3 failures with it included, both pre-existing specs green at --workers=1. Caveat on the evidence: OPENAI_API_KEY is unset here, so auto-resolve-ticket throws and the recorded seed race never fired - it is untested rather than disproven.

reasons: AC1: All 12 approved instances assert their observable and pass at component level. But a real browser shows the selected status never reaching the URL: in ATT-2a4de7cca678, after chooseStatus(page, 'Open') followed immediately by Next, expect(page).toHaveURL(/status=open/) received 'http://localhost:5174/tickets?page=2' and retried 8 times over 5s. The failure snapshot shows the status combobox back at 'All statuses' on page 2 of an unfiltered list. Suspect path traced: client/src/pages/TicketsPage.tsx write() serialises a render-snapshot params object and calls setSearchParams(value) rather than the functional-updater form, so two writes issued from one committed render clobber each other. Competing reading that cannot be separated by reading alone: the Radix option click was itself lost. Same observable either way - a selection the user made did not reach the URL.

AC3: All 9 enumerated instances pass, including the re-render and refetch traps. The gap is real-browser only: in ATT-2a4de7cca678, with status and sort already settled in the URL, Next was clicked and toHaveURL(/page=2/) failed on '?status=open&sortBy=subject&sortOrder=desc'. The snapshot shows 'Showing 1-10 of 22 tickets', 'Page 1 of 3' and Next ENABLED, so the button was clickable and the write never happened. The spec's own named excuse for this test - auto-resolve stealing page 2 - is ruled out: OPENAI_API_KEY is unset per environmentProfile and 22 open tickets across 3 pages are in the snapshot. Candidate mechanism: client/src/pages/TicketsTable.tsx renders the whole pagination footer under {!isLoading && !error && ...} and useQuery sets no placeholderData, so every new query key destroys and re-creates the Next button; a click landing on the pre-transition node reaches no React handler.

AC4: The two instances the spec assigns to E2E as their only proof both failed: CASE-e51a15eb56e6 and CASE-8e3d236b21a9. Neither failure reached its own claim - both died on the setup step - so the retrace restore and the nav-link destination are unproven as well as failing. The producer and consumer halves are genuinely asserted at component level (exact listSearch on the Link state, and an exact href on the detail back link), so the mechanism works in jsdom; what is unproven is the behaviour in a real browser.

AC8: All 6 approved instances verified. The ambiguity is the sort pair, and both readings are honest. Reading A, which the spec states as the only reasonable one ('omit every value equal to its default'): when only the direction differs the URL should be '?sortOrder=asc'. Reading B, implemented in client/src/lib/ticket-list-params.ts and locked in by a unit assertion that serialize({sortBy: 'createdAt', sortOrder: 'asc'}) === 'sortBy=createdAt&sortOrder=asc': the sort is a pair, so a URL that mentions sorting names both halves, and sortBy=createdAt therefore appears while equalling its default. No approved case covers 'only the direction differs', so neither the case set nor the plan adjudicates it. The code and the spec text disagree.
